dialogue.agent: Hello, how may I help you today?

dialogue.user: Hi! I’m looking for a book, but I’m on a pretty tight budget. Can you recommend something good that costs $15 or less? I’m mainly interested in something that has decent quality—so I’d like it to have an average rating of at least 3 out of 5. What do you have that might fit those criteria?
dialogue.agent:
Here are some options under $15, all with an average rating of 5.0 (from 1–3 reviews):

- "The Blackwater Chronicle: A Narrative of an Expedition into the Land of Canaan in Randolph County, Virginia" – $14.95
- "Thoughts on Small Boat Racing" – $8.98
- "Hit The Road!: A Badass Mom's Guide For Families who Want to Travel the World" – $12.99
- "From Apathy to Harmony: A Collection of Poems" – $5.50
- "Musings & Vignettes: A sketchbook for thoughts and illustrations" – $5.00

Are you interested in any particular genre, or would you like a brief description of any of these titles?

dialogue.user: Thanks for the quick reply! I think I’d like a little more information before deciding. Could you please give me a brief description of “From Apathy to Harmony: A Collection of Poems” and “Hit The Road!: A Badass Mom's Guide For Families who Want to Travel the World”? I’m not really picky about genre, just want to get a sense of what these books are about.
dialogue.agent:
Here’s a summary of each book:

- "From Apathy to Harmony: A Collection of Poems" ($5.50, 5.0 rating, 1 review): This anthology by Camille Peasley is a poetic journey out of apathy and depression, sharing personal reflections and growth. The poems are ordered to reflect moving from a difficult period into a more hopeful mindset.

- "Hit The Road!: A Badass Mom's Guide For Families who Want to Travel the World" ($12.99, 5.0 rating, 3 reviews): This book offers inspiration and practical advice for families interested in traveling long-term. It covers logistics, remote working, schooling on the road, travel emergencies, and interviews with real traveling families, making it ideal for anyone considering “Worldschooling” or global family adventures.

Would you like reviews from other readers on either of these, or is there one that interests you more?

result.title: From Apathy to Harmony: A Collection of Poems
result.features: "For a couple years I've been stuck in a personal rut and letting myself wallow in apathy and depression. This anthology is about a journey, and I've chosen the poems and ordered them so that they reflect that journey. For me these poems are about remembering when I was at my worst, remembering why I stepped out of my rut, out of depression, and why I want to continue to try to move forward." -written by the author, Camille Peasley

result.title: Hit The Road!: A Badass Mom's Guide For Families who Want to Travel the World
result.features: You don’t have to decide whether to work OR travel...you can do both! Hit the Road! is a book to inspire families who have always dreamed of traveling with their children. Whether for a year or a lifetime, if you’re a single mother of one or a traditional family of five, this book explains how to take those first steps to get on the road, and what to do once you’re there. It looks at logistics and schooling, remote working, and how to meet others, travel emergencies, and much more.Filled with inspiration, practical information, and personal anecdotes – interviews with traveling families who share how they did it and their lessons learned – Hit the Road! will educate you about the fast-growing community of “Worldschooling” and traveling families. If you are someone who marvels at other families traveling the world and imagine doing the same, then this book is for you! So many families are already doing it... you can too.

Just to confirm, does "From Apathy to Harmony: A Collection of Poems" have an average rating of 3 or higher? And are there any major content warnings or anything else I should be aware of before deciding?
